label: Speaker in 3D — captions behind and in front
description: THE PERSON with captions living in the room around them (speaker and creator-cut films): a BIG key word stands BEHIND the head (the person's cut-out covers its middle, the letters peek out either side), SMALL words build word by word beside the face and STACK as rows on their side ("I've learned / that people / what you said") until a wipe or a big word on that side clears them, a RING carries its phrase once as a smile-curve across the chest (turning; the ends curl behind the person), one CAMERA push/orbit moves it all with the text at its own depths (parallax), and SILHOUETTE WIPES sweep the person's black cut-out across the frame between thoughts. It IS the speaker layer: src 'speaker' (it draws the take itself -- the room copy under the alpha cut-out, which it asks the matte for). Every `at` takes a word anchor ("@forget"). Use it for the beats where the WORDS are the point -- a line with one word worth feeling. Before the take exists the captions still perform. One per scene; do not also cast a video speaker in the same scene.

until.label: Until (default: the next line of its kind; a wipe clears everything; small lines stay stacked until a wipe, a big word on their side, or three rows)

layer.label: Layer (default: big behind, small in front)

color.label: Color (default: accent for big/ring, white for small)

size.label: Size (fraction of frame height; big 0.3 -- a centred one scales to ~70% of the width; small 0.046; ring 0.062, fitted to its arc)

wipes.label: Silhouette wipes (the person's black cut-out sweeping across)
